The '''Young Turks''' were a group of leading scientists who worked at [[Bell Labs]], who were insatiably curious about the science behind communications. Many of them were encouraged to take risks, free from the responsibilities of applying for grants or from teaching.<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/plugged-in/building-new-homes-for-energy-innovation/
| title=Building New Homes for Energy Innovation
| publisher=[[Scientific American]]
| author1=Varun Mehra
| author2=Sebastien Lounis
| date=2015-02-27
| access-date=2025-09-10}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url=http://www.thedeal.com/thedealeconomy/jon-gertners-the-idea-factory.php
| title=Jon Gertner's 'The Idea Factory'
| date=2012-06-19
| author=Robert Teitelman
| publisher=[[The Deal (magazine)|The Deal]]
| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150624044133/http://www.thedeal.com/thedealeconomy/jon-gertners-the-idea-factory.php
| archive-date=2015-06-24
| url-status=dead
| access-date=2025-09-10}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/jon-gertner-idea-factory_b_1612463
| title=Jon Gertner's 'The Idea Factory'
| date=2012-06-20
| author=Robert Teitelman
| publisher=[[Huffington Post]]
| access-date=2025-09-10}}</ref> "We were first-class troublemakers," [[Richard Hamming]] later recalled. "We did unconventional things in unconventional ways and still got valuable results. Thus management had to tolerate us and let us alone a lot of the time."<ref name="IEEE">{{cite web
| url=https://history.computer.org/pioneers/hamming.html
| title=Computer Pioneers – Richard Wesley Hamming
| author=J. A. N. Lee
| publisher=[[IEEE Computer Society]]
| access-date=2025-09-10}}</ref>
